reasons: Classification is correct: Section 4.1 gives a mutual 90-day exit (at fallback on notice mechanics, appropriately not redlined), but the Section 4.2(a) Termination Payment (50% of trailing 12-month Net Sales above $800,000, payable only by the Company) is an early-termination charge that materially exceeds the fallback cap of three months' fees — arithmetic against the Section 3.1 revenue share (30% of Net Sales above $11,000/month) confirms the formula can exceed a full year of fees, so the clause fails the fallback and is a genuine deviation, not an acceptable-fallback over-flag.

Redline is minimal and actionable: it preserves the original formula and inserts only a proviso capping the payment at three months' Section 3.1 fees plus a carve-out where the Company terminates for HDI's breach or under Section 1.6 — the smallest edit that reaches the playbook fallback; no unnecessary addition of a Customer convenience right (one already exists) and no unwarranted deletion of HDI's symmetric right, which is effective only at renewal.

Failed deterministic checks are not substantive: the 'Customer convenience termination present' regex misses the phrasing in Section 4.1 (termination by 'either Party' on 90 days' notice), and the 0.896 changed-character ratio reflects an append-only insertion that leaves the original wording intact.

Comment is accurate, correctly cites the preferred position (no penalty, pro-rata refund) while offering the three-month fee cap fallback, notes the absence of prepaid fees, and stays within the required concise first-person-plural tone with the [Playbook] prefix.
